correctness.rationale: Three-round EF on vertex-transitive graphs is equivalent to equality of all second-vertex adjacency indicators and sets of possible third-vertex adjacency masks. This lemma follows by back-and-forth after a transitive first move. Explicit k-set exchanges prove the masks for d=1,2,>=3, including the unique J(6,3) failure of the 00 bit. For k=2 outside-ground-element counts give exact transitions at n=5,6; complete graph cases are immediate. The seven signatures differ, so the proof establishes universal quantifiers. Direct enumeration of 34 finite instances checks the table but is not substituted for infinite proof.

value.rationale: An exact natural low-depth logical classification of the complete balanced two-parameter Johnson-graph family is a finite-model-theoretic structural invariant. It isolates a universal rank-three collapse across infinitely many graph orders and subset widths together with one exceptional higher-width parameter pair, not merely an arbitrary finite test. This information is useful for depth-three definability and for calibrating comparisons with stronger counting/metric logics. The k=2 portion is not represented as new.
